title: Submission targets
description: Places that accept a submission, screened but not yet proven to publish a link. This is the first-pass resource library: relevance and authority never gate entry here, only reachability and the existence of a route. A row graduates into free-channels.json once an actual placement is observed on a live page — until then it makes no claim about rel, anchor, or indexability.

domain.description: Registrable domain, no scheme, no www.

route.description: The submission URL that was actually reached, after redirects.

kind.description: What the site is, judged from the page itself — never from the source list's blurb.

gate.description: The EARLIEST thing standing between you and a submitted form. Kept for sorting and for the single-answer question 'what stops me here first'. For selecting a batch, use `cohort`; for the complete picture, use `gates`.

price.description: Verbatim as printed on the page, with its currency. Null unless read.

status.description: usable = reachable and a submission route exists. gated = route exists but needs a human (interactive CAPTCHA, personal contact, reciprocal link). dead rows are kept only when a previously usable row died; never import a source's dead rows.

sourceList.description: Where the lead came from. A source is provenance, never evidence.

finalUrl.description: After redirects. A directory that now 200s onto an unrelated product is dead, and only this field catches it.

gates.description: EVERY gate observed on the route, not just the first. A site can want an account AND a CAPTCHA AND an email confirmation; recording only the earliest one loses the cost of the other two, and the cost is what decides which batch it belongs to. Must contain `gate`.

cohort.description: Which run this target belongs in, derived from `gates`. The point of the field is that a campaign is planned per cohort: `open` needs nobody, `captcha` needs a human present, `account` needs credentials decided up front, `personal-contact` needs the owner's real details. Mixing cohorts in one run is what makes a batch stall.

traffic.description: Measured human traffic. This is the admission gate (>= 100 monthly visits) and it is checked BEFORE any form is filled. Absent means never measured — which is not the same as zero, and not a licence to submit.

monthlyVisits.description: Null only when the source could not find the domain at all.

verdict.description: pass = >= 100 monthly visits. fail = measured but under the floor. below-floor = the data source has no record of this domain, i.e. traffic too small to measure, which counts as failing. error = the check itself broke; re-run it, do not read it as a verdict.

communityBoards.description: Community leaderboards that mentioned this domain — provenance and ranking signal, not evidence. A row here says 'this many voters recommended submitting here', never 'this link was placed'.

submitterNote.description: Submitter's own reasoning, verbatim, truncated to 500 chars.

boardEntryUrl.description: URL as originally written in the board entry.
